notes.meaning: Young Samuel carried out his daily duties for the Lord under Eli's supervision. In those days, messages and visions from God were very rare. Because the priests and the people had grown corrupt, God seldom spoke directly to the nation.

Eli was resting in his usual room for the night. His eyesight had grown so dim with old age that he was nearly blind. Because of this, he relied on young Samuel to sleep close by and help him when needed.

Samuel was lying down near the sacred tent where the ark of the covenant was kept. The gold lampstand burned through the night and had not yet gone out, which shows this happened just before dawn. Even in Israel's darkest spiritual hour, God's light had not been completely extinguished.
The Lord called Samuel by name in the quiet of the night. The boy immediately responded, ready to help. Samuel showed a willing heart to serve without delay.
Samuel ran quickly to Eli, assuming the elderly priest had called for him. Eli explained that he had not called and told the boy to go back to bed. Samuel obediently returned to his sleeping place.

The Lord called Samuel a second time, and the boy got up and went to Eli once more. Eli spoke kindly to him, calling him his son, and repeated that he had not called. He instructed Samuel to lie down again.

Samuel did not yet recognize God's voice because the Lord had never spoken directly to him before. He had been taught the Scriptures and served faithfully, but direct prophetic revelation was brand new to him. God was just beginning to introduce Himself to Samuel as a prophet.

differ.view: Samuel had not yet been spiritually converted, and he came to personal saving faith during this night.
Samuel already possessed true personal faith and devotion, but had not yet experienced God revealing prophecies to him.

notes.meaning: The Lord called Samuel a third time, and the boy went straight to Eli again. After three identical visits, Eli finally realized that it was the Lord calling the boy. God graciously repeated His call until the message got through.

Eli told Samuel to go back to bed and gave him the exact words to say if the voice returned. He taught the boy to say, 'Speak, Lord, for Your servant is listening.' We should approach God with that same quiet willingness to listen and obey.

The Lord came and stood there, calling out twice, 'Samuel! Samuel!' Samuel answered humbly as Eli had instructed, leaving out only the divine name since he was filled with awe. He placed himself in the posture of an attentive servant ready to receive God's word.

differ.view: The Lord standing there may have been a visible appearance of Jesus before His birth in Bethlehem.

notes.meaning: The Lord warned Samuel that He was about to do something startling in Israel. The coming events would be so terrible that the ears of everyone who heard about them would tingle with shock. God was preparing to judge the nation and its religious leaders.

The Lord declared that He would bring about every judgment He had previously announced against Eli's family. Once God started this work of punishment, He would carry it through from start to finish. His patience had lasted long, but His justice would be thorough.

God explained that Eli's family was facing permanent judgment for sins Eli knew all about. Eli's sons had openly disgraced holy things and blasphemed God, yet Eli never removed them from office or restrained them. Leaders and parents share the blame when they refuse to correct evil they have the power to stop.

The Lord swore a solemn oath that no animal sacrifices or grain gifts could ever turn away this punishment. Eli's sons had deliberately hardened their hearts and despised the sacred offerings, so the time for mercy had run out. God's decision to remove the priesthood from Eli's family was final.

Samuel stayed in bed until morning and then quietly did his usual chore of opening the sanctuary doors. Even after receiving a revelation from God, he remained humble and attentive to ordinary work. He was terrified to tell the aged priest about the severe judgment God had spoken.

Eli called out to the boy, warmly calling him 'Samuel, my son.' Samuel answered right away, showing his usual readiness to serve his mentor. The tender words between them made the hard message all the more painful to deliver.

Eli asked Samuel to tell him the Lord's message and urged him not to hide anything. He placed Samuel under a strict curse, asking God to punish the boy severely if he held back a single word. Eli suspected the news was bad, but he still wanted the full truth.

Samuel told Eli every word of the message without holding anything back. Eli replied with quiet submission, saying, 'He is the Lord; let Him do what is good in His eyes.' Eli recognized God's right to rule and accepted the sentence against his family.

differ.view: Many see Eli's words as a model of godly humility before God's sovereign will, but some view his reaction as spiritual laziness since he never repented or begged for mercy.

notes.meaning: Samuel grew into manhood, and the Lord remained with him to guide and strengthen him. God made sure that every prophecy Samuel delivered came completely true. When a person stays faithful in small things, God honors them with greater responsibility.

All the people of Israel, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the deep south, realized that Samuel was a trustworthy prophet. His calling was confirmed throughout the entire nation. God provided His people with a reliable guide during a chaotic time.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars observe that this is the first time the text gives Samuel the formal title of prophet, even though he had been performing priestly work without ever receiving the title of priest.

notes.meaning: The Lord continued to make regular appearances at Shiloh, revealing His will to Samuel through prophetic messages. The long season of spiritual silence had come to an end. God once again spoke openly to His people through His chosen messenger.
